statement: Two polling organizations surveyed random samples of likely voters in two different towns about a proposed tax. In Town P, $54\%$ of those surveyed supported the tax, with a margin of error of $3$ percentage points. In Town Q, $49\%$ of those surveyed supported the tax, with a margin of error of $4$ percentage points. Which conclusion is best supported by these results?

choices.text: The percent of likely voters who support the tax is greater in Town P than in Town Q.
choices.misconception: I compared 54% with 49% and ignored the margins of error, but the plausible ranges, 51% to 57% and 45% to 53%, overlap, so Town P is not clearly higher.

choices.text: The percent of likely voters who support the tax is exactly $5$ percentage points greater in Town P than in Town Q.
choices.misconception: I subtracted the sample percents and treated 5 points as the exact difference, but each sample percent is only an estimate of its town's true percent.

choices.text: A majority of likely voters in each of the two towns support the tax.
choices.misconception: I saw that both plausible ranges reach above 50%, but Town Q's range goes as low as 45%, so a majority there is not supported.

choices.text: It is plausible that the percent of likely voters who support the tax is the same in both towns.

hints: Each margin of error turns a sample percent into a range of plausible values.
Write the interval of plausible values for each town, then check whether the two intervals share any values.
Town P: $51\%$ to $57\%$. Town Q: $45\%$ to $53\%$. Look at the values from $51\%$ to $53\%$.

solutions.reliable: For Town P the plausible values are $54 \pm 3$, from $51\%$ to $57\%$. For Town Q they are $49 \pm 4$, from $45\%$ to $53\%$. The intervals overlap from $51\%$ to $53\%$, so a value such as $52\%$ is plausible for both towns. The results therefore do not show that support differs between the towns, and it is plausible that the two percents are equal. A majority is not supported for Town Q, whose interval includes values below $50\%$, and no exact difference can be claimed from two estimates.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
